Next Introduction.exp: Introduction to Next and its ecosystem.

Pages: The Pages Router is the original routing system in Next.js. Pages in the pages directory automatically become routes based on their file name, with index.js mapping to the root and nested folders creating nested paths.

export default function Home() { return

Hello World

; }
Routing: Next.js supports dynamic routes using bracket syntax like [id].js. Links are created using the next/link component for client-side navigation with prefetching.
App Router: The App Router (app directory) is the modern routing system using React Server Components by default. Routes are defined by folders with page.js files, and layouts can be nested via layout.js.

Next Data.exp: Working with data and APIs in Next.

Vercel: Vercel is the official deployment platform for Next.js, offering zero-config deploys from Git, automatic HTTPS, edge functions, and preview deployments for every pull request.
Docker: Next.js apps can be containerized with Docker for deployment on any container orchestration platform. A multi-stage Dockerfile optimizes for build speed and image size.

FROM node:18-alpine AS base
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["npm", "start"]
Self-hosted: Next.js supports self-hosting on any Node.js server using the standalone output mode. The standalone folder includes only production dependencies, minimizing deployment size.

getServerSideProps: getServerSideProps runs on every request on the server, fetching data before rendering the page. It is used when you need fresh data on each request or access to request-time information like cookies.
getStaticProps: getStaticProps runs at build time to fetch data for static generation. The generated HTML is reused for each request, making it ideal for content that changes infrequently.
Server Actions: Server Actions allow running server-side code directly from client components. They are functions defined with 'use server' that can be called via form actions or programmatically, handling mutations without building API routes.

SSR: Server-Side Rendering generates HTML on each request, delivering fully rendered pages to the client. This improves SEO and initial load performance at the cost of slower response times compared to static generation.
SSG: Static Site Generation pre-renders pages at build time into HTML and JSON files. These static files are served by CDN with near-instant load times, ideal for marketing pages, blogs, and documentation.

export async function getStaticProps() { return { props: {} }; }
export async function getStaticPaths() { return { paths: [], fallback: 'blocking' }; }
ISR: Incremental Static Regeneration allows updating static content after build without rebuilding the entire site. Pages are served from cache and regenerated in the background when the revalidation window expires.
CSR: Client-Side Rendering fetches data and renders content in the browser after the initial page load. This is useful for highly interactive, user-specific dashboards where SEO is not critical.

CSS Modules: CSS Modules scope styles locally to the component by generating unique class names. Files named *.module.css are automatically supported, preventing style conflicts across components.
Tailwind: Next.js integrates with Tailwind CSS out of the box. Tailwind's utility classes enable rapid styling directly in JSX, with purging of unused styles in production builds.
CSS-in-JS: CSS-in-JS libraries like styled-components and Emotion work with Next.js but require configuration. The app router requires using a registry to collect styles during server-side rendering.

REST: Next.js API routes let you build REST endpoints inside the pages/api directory. Each file exports functions matching HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) that receive req and res objects.
Middleware: Middleware runs before every request and can modify headers, redirect users, or rewrite URLs. It is defined as middleware.ts in the root of the project and executes on the Edge runtime.
Edge Functions: Edge Functions run on the Vercel Edge Network using the Edge Runtime. They provide low-latency, globally distributed execution for API routes, middleware, and server rendering.

NextAuth: NextAuth.js (now Auth.js) provides a complete authentication solution for Next.js. It supports OAuth providers, email magic links, and credentials with minimal setup using the app router.
JWT: JSON Web Tokens are commonly used for stateless authentication in Next.js. Tokens are signed server-side and verified on each request, often stored in httpOnly cookies for security.

import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';
const token = jwt.sign({ userId: user.id }, process.env.JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '7d' });
Session Management: Session management in Next.js can use database-backed sessions or JWT-based sessions via NextAuth. The session is accessed via useSession on the client or getServerSession on the server.

import { getServerSession } from 'next-auth';
const session = await getServerSession(req, res, authOptions);

Image Optimization: The next/image component automatically optimizes images with lazy loading, responsive sizes, and WebP/AVIF format conversion. Images are served via the built-in image optimizer API.

import Image from 'next/image';
<Image src='/hero.jpg' alt='Hero' width={1200} height={600} priority />
Fonts: next/font automatically optimizes and self-hosts Google Fonts and custom fonts, eliminating external requests. It supports variable fonts and subsetting for reduced bundle size.
Bundle Analysis: Next.js provides built-in bundle analysis through @next/bundle-analyzer. It generates visual reports showing the size of each JavaScript bundle and its dependencies to identify optimization targets.

Route Groups: Route groups organize routes without affecting URL paths by wrapping folder names in parentheses. They are useful for separating marketing, admin, and auth sections with different layouts.
Parallel Routes: Parallel routes render multiple pages simultaneously in the same layout using named slots. Each slot has its own loading and error states, enabling complex dashboard and feed layouts.
Intercepting Routes: Intercepting routes overlay content from another route within the current layout using (..) syntax. They are commonly used for modal previews that render as full pages on hard refresh.

app/
  feed/
    page.tsx
    (..)photo/[id]/page.tsx  // intercepts /photo/[id] from /feed
  photo/
    [id]/page.tsx

Static Metadata: The metadata object export defines page-level SEO data including title, description, Open Graph, and Twitter cards. It supports static values and template-based title generation.
Dynamic Metadata: Dynamic metadata is generated with the generateMetadata function that receives route params and search params, enabling SEO data based on fetched content.
Metadata API: Next.js provides a comprehensive Metadata API covering Open Graph, Twitter cards, JSON-LD structured data, manifest, icons, robots, sitemaps, and alternate language links.

Turbopack: Turbopack is Next.js's Rust-based incremental bundler replacing webpack in development. It provides near-instant HMR, sub-second cold starts, and incremental computation for large projects.
Partial Prerendering: Partial Prerendering (PPR) combines static and dynamic rendering on the same page. Static shell content is served instantly while dynamic holes stream in after rendering on the server.
Instrumentation: Instrumentation hooks allow running code on server startup. The register() function in instrumentation.ts is useful for OpenTelemetry tracing, metrics setup, and infrastructure initialization.

Middleware, i18n & Redirects: Next.js Middleware runs before every request, enabling redirects, rewrites, geolocation-based routing, and authentication checks. Middleware uses the Edge Runtime (fast, global). Internationalization (i18n) with next-intl or built-in middleware-based routing. Redirects in next.config.js handle legacy URLs. Rewrites proxy requests to external APIs without CORS issues. Middleware uses NextRequest and NextResponse. Avoid heavy computation in middleware — it runs on every request.
Next.js Caching & Performance: Next.js provides multi-layered caching: Full Route Cache (static HTML cached at edge), Data Cache (fetch results cached with next.revalidate), Router Cache (client-side cache for 30s), and React Cache (server component deduplication). revalidatePath and revalidateTag purge caches on-demand. generateStaticParams pre-builds pages at build time. ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) updates static pages after build. loading.tsx provides per-route loading states. The next/image component optimizes images with lazy loading and WebP/AVIF conversion.
